title: CRESTOR (rosuvastatin) tablets, for oral use: full prescribing information
authors: US Food and Drug Administration (labelling submitted by AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP)
journal: US Food and Drug Administration approved prescribing information, via DailyMed; version 19, effective 23 September 2026; sections 4 to 8
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement
result: Warnings: myopathy and rhabdomyolysis, with acute kidney injury secondary to myoglobinuria and rare fatalities; risk factors are age 65 years or older, uncontrolled hypothyroidism, renal impairment, interacting drugs and higher dose; myopathy risk greater on 40 mg; Asian patients may be at higher risk, with about 2-fold median exposure against White controls; exposure raised to a clinically significant extent in severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) without haemodialysis. Rare immune-mediated necrotising myopathy. Transaminases above 3 times the upper limit of normal in 1.1% on rosuvastatin against 0.5% on placebo in pooled placebo-controlled trials; rare postmarketing fatal and non-fatal hepatic failure. Dipstick-positive proteinuria and microscopic haematuria, more frequent on 40 mg, generally transient, clinical significance unknown. Increases in HbA1c and fasting glucose that in some instances exceed the threshold for diagnosis of diabetes; in JUPITER (8901 per group, mean 2 years) diabetes was reported in 2.8% on rosuvastatin 20 mg against 2.3% on placebo and mean HbA1c rose by 0.1%. METEOR (rosuvastatin 40 mg, n=700, against placebo, n=281, mean 1.7 years): ALT above 3 times the upper limit of normal 2.2% against 0.7%, increased creatine phosphokinase 2.6% against 0.7%. Children aged 10 to 17 with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia: creatine kinase above 10 times the upper limit of normal in 4 of 130 on rosuvastatin against 0 of 46 on placebo. Postmarketing reports: thrombocytopenia; hepatitis, jaundice, fatal and non-fatal hepatic failure; immune-mediated necrotising myopathy; peripheral neuropathy; cognitive impairment, generally non-serious and reversible, onset 1 day to years, median resolution 3 weeks; new-onset or exacerbated myasthenia gravis with recurrence on rechallenge; depression; sleep disorders including insomnia and nightmares; gynaecomastia; interstitial lung disease; drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS); lichenoid drug eruption. Pregnancy: may cause fetal harm based on the mechanism of action; breastfeeding not recommended; limited case reports show rosuvastatin in human milk.
